records.question: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
search_queries: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
records.answer:
As a graduate student, you need to be registered for **at least 9 credit hours per term** to be considered full-time.

However, keep in mind that only **3 credits of online or distance coursework** can count toward this full-time minimum. So you'll need at least **6 credits in face-to-face or hybrid format** plus up to 3 online credits to meet the 9-credit requirement.

If you cannot enroll full-time, you can request [less than full-time (LTFT) approval](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/less-than-full-time) from ISSS, but you must get written permission **before the term begins**.

Source: [Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)

records.question: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?

- **Graduate students** must take at least 6 credits in face-to-face or hybrid format (to reach the 9-credit full-time minimum)

**Important note:** Hybrid classes count as in-person for immigration purposes, so you can use them to meet your face-to-face requirement.

If you need an exception, you must get written permission from ISSS before the term begins.

records.question: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
search_queries: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?

According to ISSS, you can work **no more than 20 hours per week on campus while school is in session**.

This limit applies to F-1 and J-1 students maintaining valid status. You're also required to ensure that on-campus work doesn't impact your academic performance or ability to attend classes.

- During approved vacation terms, you may work over 20 hours per week
- If you're on co-op, on-campus employment is still limited to 20 hours per week and must not interfere with your co-op responsibilities
- You must maintain valid F-1/J-1 status and not have graduated to be eligible

records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
**Currently, F-1 students have a 60-day grace period** after their program ends. During this time, you can remain in the U.S. to pack, prepare to leave, or travel within the country—but you cannot work or study.

However, **this is changing.** The Department of Homeland Security published a final rule in July 2026 that would reduce the F-1 grace period from 60 days to 30 days. A U.S. District Court postponed the effective date of this rule in September 2026, so the current 60-day grace period is still in effect, but you should confirm the current status with [ISSS](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

**Key points:**
- The grace period applies after your program ends or after your post-completion OPT ends
- If you're applying for OPT, you must file your application *before* your grace period ends to remain in valid status while the application is pending
- If you don't apply for OPT, secure a status extension, or depart during the grace period, you'll begin accruing unlawful presence

For details on your specific situation, contact an [ISSS advisor](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

**Standard OPT**: You're allowed **12 months total per degree level** (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate). You can use this before graduation (Pre-Completion OPT) or after (Post-Completion OPT).

**Important accrual rules:**
- **Pre-Completion part-time OPT**: counts at 50% (e.g., 6 months part-time = 3 months deducted)

records.question: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
search_queries: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
records.answer:
On Post-Completion OPT, you can be unemployed for a maximum of **90 days** (including weekends).

**Key points:**

- Each day from when your OPT authorization begins until it ends that you don't have qualifying employment counts toward this limit.
- If you reach 90 days of unemployment, you must take action before exceeding the limit—such as finding employment, transferring to another school, changing your educational level, or departing the U.S.
- Exceeding 90 days of unemployment violates your F-1 status and can have serious consequences, including termination of your SEVIS record and loss of valid immigration status.
- You must report any unemployment to ISSS.

If you later apply for the 2-year STEM OPT Extension, you'll be permitted an additional 60 days of unemployment (150 days total combined with your initial 12-month period).

For concerns about meeting employment requirements, contact your ISSS advisor via [https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

Source: [Optional Practical Training (OPT)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)

records.question: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?

No, you do not need a job offer to apply for OPT. However, there's an important condition for **Post-Completion OPT**:

**Pre-Completion OPT:** No job offer required. If you don't work during this period, you simply lose that time from your 12-month OPT eligibility.

**Post-Completion OPT:** No job offer required to apply, but you are **expected to actively seek employment in your field of study and be employed for at least nine months** after your OPT starts. Additionally, there is a 90-day aggregate limit on unemployment while on Post-Completion OPT. If you exceed this limit without taking action (like transferring to another school, changing educational level, or departing the U.S.), you risk violating your F-1 status.

records.question: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
search_queries: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
No, self-employment is not eligible for a STEM OPT extension. According to [ISSS](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension), the regulations require that you must have a bona fide employer-employee relationship with an employer to obtain a STEM OPT extension.

However, you **can** be self-employed during regular OPT (the initial 12-month Post-Completion OPT), provided you work full-time and can prove you have proper business licenses and are actively engaged in a business related to your degree program.

If you're interested in starting a business while on STEM OPT, you could explore whether a start-up business could employ you as an employee (rather than you being self-employed), though all regulatory requirements would still need to be met.

# Transferring Your SEVIS Record to Another University

- **If you're a J-1 student on academic training:** transfer before your DS-2019 expires

## What Ends on Transfer
Any employment authorization (on-campus work, CPT, OPT, etc.) automatically terminates on your transfer release date.

To apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons, follow these steps:

1. **Get a medical letter**: Have a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or licensed clinical psychologist write a letter on official letterhead recommending you for less than full-time (LTFT) status for a specific term. The letter must state that in their medical opinion, you cannot attend classes full-time (or at all) during that term. 3. **Wait for approval**: ISSS will review your documents and email you with a decision. Do not drop your courses until you receive approval.

**Important limits**: You can receive up to 12 aggregate months of medical LTFT per program level, and you must enroll in at least 1 course if it's your final term.

# Applying for STEM OPT Extension

The STEM OPT extension is a 24-month training period for F-1 students with STEM degrees. Here are the key steps:

## Application Steps

**Step 1: Complete Form I-983**
Download it from [DHS Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/stem-opt-hub/additional-resources/form-i-983-overview) and follow the [instructions [PDF]](https://www.ice.gov/doclib/sevis/pdf/i983Instructions.pdf).

**Step 2: Request a STEM OPT I-20 from ISSS**
Email isss@drexel.edu with:
- Completed [STEM OPT Request Form [PDF]](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/~/media/Drexel/EMSS-Site-Group/StudentLife/Documents/international-student-support/forms/stem-opt-request.pdf)
- Completed Form I-983
- STEM OPT Processing Fee Receipt
- Scans: current OPT EAD card (front/back), passport (valid 6+ months), official STEM transcript
- Most recent [I-94](https://i94.cbp.dhs.gov/I94)

**Step 3: File I-765 to USCIS Online**
Once ISSS approves your request, you'll receive the I-20 and instructions to file online with USCIS.

## Critical Deadlines

- **Send documents to ISSS at least 30 days before your current OPT EAD expires**
- **USCIS must receive your I-765 within 60 days of when ISSS prints your I-20**
- **USCIS must receive your application before your OPT EAD expires**

You can apply up to 90 days before your OPT end date. See [STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension) for more details.

records.question: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
search_queries: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
records.answer:
# CPT vs. OPT

**CPT (Curricular Practical Training)** and **OPT (Optional Practical Training)** are both off-campus work authorizations for F-1 students, but they differ in purpose and timing:

## CPT
- **Purpose:** Required part of your curriculum (internship, co-op, practicum, etc.)
- **Timing:** During your program, driven by academic requirements
- **Driven by:** Program curriculum, not your choice for employment
- **Full-time limit:** Using 364+ days of full-time CPT makes you ineligible for OPT
- **Part-time CPT:** Doesn't affect OPT eligibility

## OPT
- **Purpose:** Gain work experience related to your degree after (or before completing) your studies
- **Timing:** Before graduation (Pre-Completion OPT) or after (Post-Completion OPT)
- **Driven by:** Your choice to gain professional experience
- **Job offer:** Not required to apply
- **Post-Completion requirement:** You must actively seek and be employed in your field for at least 9 months

**Key difference:** CPT is curriculum-driven and required for your program; OPT is optional and for gaining practical experience.

For more details, see [CPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt) and [OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) pages.

records.question: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?

CPT can affect your OPT eligibility, but only if you do **full-time CPT for one year (364 days) or more**. Here's what matters:

- **Full-time CPT for less than 364 days** does **not** affect OPT eligibility

# Form I-983

The **Form I-983** is a training plan required for the STEM OPT extension. Here's what you need to know:

## What it is
The I-983 documents the training you'll receive during your STEM OPT extension. It's completed by you and your employer together.

## Where to get it
Download the Form I-983 from [DHS Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/stem-opt-hub/additional-resources/form-i-983-overview), and refer to the [Form I-983 Instructions [PDF]](https://www.ice.gov/doclib/sevis/pdf/i983Instructions.pdf) for guidance on filling it out.

- **To apply for STEM OPT extension**: Email a completed I-983 to isss@drexel.edu along with other documents to request your STEM OPT Request I-20 (see [STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)).
- **During your extension**: Complete self-evaluations within the I-983 at 12 months and at the end of your STEM period.
- **For employment changes**: Submit a completed I-983 whenever you change employers or your employment details change.

## Important note
The I-983 is **not** submitted to USCIS—only to ISSS.

For specific questions about completing the form, contact [ISSS](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

# 212(e) Two-Year Home Country Requirement

## Who it applies to

You're subject to the 212(e) two-year home country physical presence requirement if you're a J-1 exchange visitor and either:

- Your program participation was financed in whole or in part (directly or indirectly) by a U.S. government agency or your home country's government, **or**
- At the time you got J-1 status, you were a national of a country the U.S. Department of State designated as needing people with your specialized skills.

## What it means

After your J-1 program ends, you must be physically present in your home country (or last country of legal permanent residence) for **at least 2 years total** before you can:
- Become a lawful permanent resident (green card)
- Change to another visa status in the U.S.

## Can it be waived?

Yes, under certain conditions. However, **ISSS cannot help with J-1 waivers** due to conflict of interest. You must apply directly through the [U.S. Department of State](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/exchange/waiver-of-the-exchange-visitor.html).

**Important:** Waiver applications can take a year or longer to process. Once approved, you lose eligibility for J-1 extensions, transfers, and new J-1 visas. A waiver also doesn't automatically extend your legal U.S. stay.

For details specific to your situation, contact an [ISSS advisor](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

**Sources:** [J-1 Exchange Visitors](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/j1-scholars), [New International Students](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/new-international-students)

# H-1B Cap-Gap Extension

The H-1B cap-gap is the period between when your OPT (or STEM OPT) ends and your H-1B status begins. If you meet the conditions, your work authorization can be automatically extended during this time.

## Eligibility

You're eligible for H-1B cap-gap if:
- Your employer files an H-1B petition for you **on or after April 1** with a change of status to H-1B starting **October 1**
- You're still within your OPT/STEM OPT authorization period when the petition is filed

**Important:** A recent rule change extends cap-gap protection from October 1 **as late as April 1 of the following calendar year** for timely filed petitions.

## How to Apply for a Cap-Gap Extension I-20

1. **Email ISSS** to confirm your correct employment and address information in SEVIS (this significantly affects processing speed)
2. **Email one of these documents to ISSS:**
   - For extension through June 1: a statement from your employer that the H-1B application was properly filed, with proof of delivery to USCIS
   - For extension beyond June 1: a scanned USCIS receipt or proof the H-1B petition is wait-listed

ISSS will email you when your new I-20 is processed.

**Note:** The 90-day unemployment limit continues during cap-gap.

For details, see [Optional Practical Training (OPT)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) and [STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension).

The process depends on whether you're applying for **CPT** or **OPT**:

## For OPT (if your internship is optional):

Submit your application to ISSS, who will forward it to USCIS. Be aware that **USCIS can take 90 days or longer** to process. You can check current processing times on the [USCIS case processing page](https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times).

# Traveling While OPT Is Pending

Travel while OPT is pending depends on **which type of OPT** you're applying for and **when** in the process you are.

## Post-Completion OPT (after graduation)

**During the 60-day grace period:** Traveling is "slightly risky," but most students have successfully re-entered with proper documents. Carry:
- Valid passport
- Valid F-1 visa sticker (unless from Canada or Bermuda)
- I-20 with OPT recommendation and travel signature (not older than 6 months)
- OPT Receipt Notice from USCIS (proof you applied)

**Key rule:** As long as USCIS **receives** your application before your 60-day grace period ends, your F-1 status stays active while it's pending—you can remain in the U.S. even after 60 days pass.

## Pre-Completion OPT

You may travel and re-enter according to general F-1 student travel requirements.

## STEM OPT Extension (pending approval)

If your current OPT **has not expired** yet, you should be able to re-enter. If your current OPT **has expired**, traveling is risky—Customs and Border Protection makes the final decision on entry, and ISSS cannot guarantee re-entry.

Carry the same documents as above, plus an expired OPT EAD card and a letter from your employer.

**Recommendation:** Consult with an ISSS advisor about your specific situation before traveling.
